standard.title: Phthalic Anhydride, Technical — Specification (Third Revision)

sectional_committee.name: Organic Chemicals, Alcohols and Allied Products Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, sampling guidelines, and testing methods for technical-grade phthalic anhydride suitable for industrial applications—such as the manufacture of plasticizers, alkyd resins, dyes, pigments, pharmaceuticals, and polyester resins. It covers both solid forms (including flakes, pellets, or crystals) and molten liquid forms.

amendments.summary: No amendments found (this is a newly established revision in 2025, which replaces the 1987 standard and incorporates all up-to-date industry test methodologies).

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Phthalic Anhydride (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, it is a statutory offense to manufacture, import, store, distribute, or sell Phthalic Anhydride in India without a valid BIS license and the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Overseas manufacturers exporting to India must be certified under the Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial chemical compounds, as it is reserved strictly for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.
requirements: Every conforming bag or container of Phthalic Anhydride must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's license number (CM/L).

Under the 2025 revision, the traditional titrimetric analysis methods specified in the older 1987 standard are replaced by the Gas Chromatography (GC) method to determine the overall chemical purity (assay minimum 99.5% by weight) and the specific volatile or oxidizable organic impurities.

To ensure maximum consumer safety and product performance, the maximum permissible limit for Naphthaquinone impurities has been significantly reduced from 5 ppm in the old standard to 1 ppm max under IS 5158:2025.
The material must possess a minimum crystallizing point of 130.8 °C (solid form), which serves as a critical indicator of overall chemical purity and dryness.

The colour of the molten material must not exceed 20 Hazen units (HU) initially, and must not exceed 50 Hazen units after standard heat treatment, evaluated via spectrophotometric or colorimetric comparison methods.
Free acidity (expressed as phthalic acid) is strictly limited (typically to <= 0.1% max) to prevent chemical instability and downstream processing issues.
Ash residue must be extremely low (typically <= 0.01% or 0.02% max), and iron (Fe) content is restricted to trace levels to prevent discoloration in downstream polymer synthesis.

Each container must be clearly and indelibly labeled with: the manufacturer's name/brand, standard designation (IS 5158), physical form (flakes, pellets, crystals, or molten), batch/lot number, net mass, month and year of manufacture, and clear safety warning labels. Due to its irritating properties and moderate fire hazard, precaution must be taken when handling; contact with skin or inhalation of dust and fumes must be avoided, and safety goggles must be worn.
